newsitem.title: ITALY: Indicted ex-SS major draws Italian pension - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Indicted ex-SS major draws Italian pension - lawyer.

text.p: A German ex-SS major due to stand trial next month for his part in Italy's worst World War Two atrocity, draws a pension for "services in the interest of the Italian state", his lawyer told a court on Friday.

Stefano Maccioni produced pension documents in a military court, which earlier ruled that the ex-officer, Karl Hass, should stand trial on April 14. Maccioni said the pension payment dated back to the 1960s.

He said it was related to the search and recovery of bodies of German soldiers in Italy and not to work Hass did for the Italian secret services after the war. Maccioni said Germany paid Hass a similar pension.
The Italian news agency ANSA said the Italian state pension was some 200,000 lire ($117) per month.
A spokesman for the state pension body, INPS, could not immediately confirm whether Hass was on the payroll, but said they were checking. Hass, 84, was not in court on Friday.

Both Hass and former SS captain Erich Priebke are accused of complicity in multiple murder for their roles in the massacre of 335 men and boys at the Ardeatine Caves near Rome on March 24, 1944. Seventy-five of the victims were Jews.
Judicial sources said the present hearing, held in a high-security courtroom inside Rome's Rebibbia prison, could decide to merge Hass's trial with Priebke's re-trial.
At Priebke's first trial which ended in August last year, a military court found the ex-SS officer guilty but freed him, citing circumstances which triggered a statute of limitations.
He was rearrested that night after relatives of the massacre victims and other protesters laid siege to the courthouse. The August verdict was quashed on appeal in October.

Hass has been under house arrest at a private clinic near Rome since last June when he fractured his pelvis trying to clamber over a hotel balcony and flee the city. Hass returned to Italy to give testimony as a witness at Priebke's first trial.
Priebke is being held at a military prison in Rome. He has been jailed since November 1995 when he was extradited from Argentina, where he had lived openly since 1948.
Priebke, 83, admits shooting two victims at the Ardeatine Caves but said he had to follow orders or be killed. Hass has also admitted a role in the massacre.
